summary: Interest on a savings account with a bank, a co-operative bank or a post office is deducted up to a limit, for an individual who is not a senior citizen and for a Hindu undivided family. Interest on a fixed or other time deposit does not count. Only the old regime allows it.

routes.name: Savings-account interest
routes.description: The savings-account interest, up to the lower limit.

disqualifiers.description: Deposit interest is not deducted in the default regime.
Unless you are a senior citizen, interest on a fixed or other time deposit is not deducted.
Interest from anyone other than a bank, a co-operative bank or a post office — a company deposit or a loan — is not deducted.
A senior citizen takes the deduction for deposit interest instead.
Where an expense is entered against the deposit interest, the deduction is not computed.

enforcedBy.reason: whether the interest is taken before or after the expense is not settled
